author: Basil of Caesarea
occasion: Basil exhorts his hearers to combine mercy with just dealing, warning that almsgiving from unjust gain is unacceptable to God and that refraining from injustice without giving to the poor is also insufficient.
argument: Basil argues that true piety requires both justice and mercy together. He first shows that those who forget God fall into injustice and inhumanity, while God's law commands both abstaining from harm and showing mercy. He then warns that alms derived from unjust gain are rejected, and urges showing mercy to the one wronged, using one's philanthropy toward that person, which fulfills 'mercy with judgment'; Zacchaeus models the combined action of repaying what was taken and giving to the poor. Finally, he teaches that Christians must give from their own labor and possessions, because mercy to the poor is service to Christ himself and will be rewarded at the judgment.

outline.move: Basil opens by contrasting the godless world's injustice with God's call to cease evil and learn to do good, and argues that justice and mercy must be joined, so the rich must examine whether their offerings come from just earnings.

He condemns giving alms from unjust gain, urges showing mercy to the one wronged by using one's philanthropy toward that person, cites Zacchaeus as the model who promised to repay fourfold and gave half to the poor, and warns that those who avoid injustice but neglect mercy are like the fruitless fig tree.

He urges giving from one's own labor and possessions, presents the Lord's counsel to one wishing to follow to sell all one's possessions for the benefit of the poor and thus follow him, and concludes with the promise that mercy to the poor is service to Christ and will be rewarded at his coming.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Zacchaeus models the combined action of repaying what was taken and giving to the poor
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὃς, προθέμενος ἀποδοῦναι τετραπλάσιον, εἴ τι ἐσυκοφάντησεν, οὕτω τῶν ὑπολειπομένων χρημάτων τὰ ἡμίση πτωχοῖς ἀπεμέρισεν
_unresolved_facts.fix: Zacchaeus promised to repay fourfold if he had extorted anything, and then (οὕτω, 'thus'/'in this way'/'thereafter') gave half of his remaining goods to the poor. The Greek does not clearly indicate simultaneous action; rather, the repayment of wrongs comes first, then the almsgiving from what remains.

_unresolved_facts.claim: presents the Lord's counsel to one wishing to follow to sell all one's possessions for the benefit of the poor and thus follow him
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Τῷ δὲ ἀκολουθεῖν βουλομένῳ, καὶ πᾶσαν πιπράσκειν τὴν οὐσίαν εἰς εὐεργεσίαν πενήτων ὁ Κύριος εἰσηγήσατο, καὶ οὕτως ἀκολουθεῖν αὐτῷ
_unresolved_facts.fix: Basil presents this as the Lord's counsel to one wishing to follow, to sell all one's possessions for the benefit of the poor and thus follow him—but this is Basil's summary/interpretation of the rich young ruler narrative, not a direct quotation. The brief should note this is Basil's paraphrase.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Paul... quoted on working to have something to share (Ephesians 4:28)
_unresolved_facts.fix: The brief identifies the Pauline quotation as Ephesians 4:28, but the source only quotes: 'Ἐργαζόμενοι φησὶ, τὸ ἀγαθὸν ταῖς χερσὶν, ἵνα ἔχητε μεταδιδόναι τῷ χρείαν ἔχοντι.' While this resembles Ephesians 4:28, Basil does not identify the specific epistle; the brief should either note this as 'cf. Ephesians 4:28' or omit the specific citation.

_unresolved_facts.claim: the righteous... introduced as the righteous marveling (θαυμασάντων) and saying
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Θαυμασάντων δὲ τῶν δικαίων καὶ εἰπόντων· Πότε ταῦτα ἐποιήσαμεν εἰς σέ, Κύριε;
_unresolved_facts.fix: The righteous are introduced as 'τῶν δικαίων' (the righteous/dikaiōn), not specifically 'marveling'—θαυμασάντων is a genitive absolute ('when they had marveled/wondered'), but the primary identification is 'the righteous' or 'the just ones' at the judgment. The voice label should be 'the righteous' or 'the just'.
